subject: Total scores of an item bank using actual responses

messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: Total scores of an item bank using actual responses
parts:
Hi Phil,

I have been using mirt package to develop an item bank, which has a total of 13 items.
At this stage, our team wanted to calculate the total scores given respondents' responses, and I have 2 specific questions below:

1) what function I should use to calculate the total scores if having 13 items' responses?

2) what if there is some missing for the 13 items, e.g. just having 12 items' responses?

Thanks for any comments/helps in advance!

Yingyi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Total scores of an item bank using actual responses
parts: On Wed, Jun 13, 2018 at 7:31 PM <yingyi....@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil,

I have been using mirt package to develop an item bank, which has a total of 13 items.
At this stage, our team wanted to calculate the total scores given respondents' responses, and I have 2 specific questions below:

1) what function I should use to calculate the total scores if having 13 items' responses?
Is this a mirt question or about general data managing? If mirt, the fscores() function. If general data, something like rowSums()
2) what if there is some missing for the 13 items, e.g. just having 12 items' responses?
In mirt that doesn't matter, it just means that there is more sampling variability in the estimates. In rowSums, you'd probably need na.rm=TRUE, or something to that extent.

Thanks for any comments/helps in advance!

Yingyi
